title: Tunk brass bands and how brotherhood has changed
summary: Barnes describes ear brass bands playing dance music in the streets, and how clubs have made musicians less friendly than when Steve died.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: What about the Tunk Brass bands? How did they play? Brass bands? The real Tunk ones, you know, they had to, you know when Rene would get a band together, say.
Oh, well it sounded like this instrument, I like a big line band. That's what it would be like.
So they played kind of the dance music but in the streets, huh?

In the streets, yeah. They played like a band, you see them bands come off with, you'll tell yourself you'll do like you want, just turn loose. See, the other ones you see them blowing at each other. See, like a man, you catch this trumpet once, play more than that trumpet, play more than that and well. That's different.
Well, who were some of the Tunk bands, Tunk Brass bands now, you know? Not the reading brass bands, but the ear brass bands. Do they have many regular ones or do they just jump up or what?

Well, I'll tell you how I teach it, it's just late or anything like that. You and his guys are working. You say that there's about two or three brass bands, but before it was different. You take for instance like that poor Steve died. Well, you take a bunch of men and say that there was personally a good friend to him. You see, when you go get sick, you want to make a little one or two hours of Steve there? Sure man. Want to buckle grandma, book a deep grass, myself, and oh, make that up and go up there and get a grandma and go up there and get them sent away. But now it's all good, you see, you've got to belong to a club and you've got to do this and you've got to rank the man. Well as I first said, no two words about it, things are different. Different from altogether from what it used to be. You catch the limitations and it's not as friendly as it used to be. Do you know the other night that I went up there? Now God knows this is true. Howard George, everybody could shake a glad hand. You know what Alfred done to me? He was continuing picking on his drum then, not touching him, he was just going to stand like he didn't hear me and he looked at me and he shook hands like that. I said, Jesus Christ, what did I do? I never told a man to come down here before Steve died. He said, God, and he said, come to see me. Well, it's all right. He said, I've got feet up and all that. It's in the hood, I was just as a sea. When you're coming to find out, I know what it was. He go and see, see, see, see, see, see, see, see, see, you die and I'm here. I listen to it when I'm laying off the ass and I'm up. I'm up. I'm feeling all right. I tell you how I do feel. I get ready right now, see, I'm going up there. See, I get ready to go up there. Time comes. I come away. See, I see you. But I'm going to go up there because I've got to find out for me. Without doing this thing, I'm really feeling right in this thing. I do that. Yeah. Mm-hm.
